description: Cross-platform fidelity threshold for alpha=4 force detection: IonQ Cambridge + FT neutral atom resource estimation

fidelity_threshold_for_alpha_detection.note: 99.99% per gate for 56 CX gates gives noise_floor=0.56%, allowing dr=4 at 3-sigma

ionq_cambridge.estimated_fidelity: ~99.3-99.5% (based on IonQ Forte, Cambridge not publicly disclosed)
ionq_cambridge.verdict: NOT_VIABLE for power-law detection. Would need >99.99% fidelity.
ionq_cambridge.action_required: Contact IonQ Cambridge team for actual fidelity spec

ft_neutral_atom.verdict: VIABLE and definitive. FT run achieves full 6-point force profile for robust alpha fit.

hypothesis_claim_vs_result.claim: Force detection at dr=1..6 requires fidelity >= 99.5%
hypothesis_claim_vs_result.result: dr=1..4 requires 99.99%; dr=1..2 requires 99.92% (Helios). Threshold is 50x tighter than claimed.
hypothesis_claim_vs_result.reason: Hypothesis used 8q N_2Q=40 estimate; actual 16q MERA has 56 CX gates, accumulating more error

resource_hierarchy_revised.1_helios_now: dr=1..2 force existence proof (NOT full power law). 99.921% fidelity, 0.57% error, QCUP PHY204 pending.
resource_hierarchy_revised.2_ionq_cambridge: dr=1 only (NOT viable for power law). Only useful if fidelity confirmed >= 99.99%.
resource_hierarchy_revised.3_ft_neutral_atom_2027: Full dr=1..6, alpha=4 fit to high precision. Definitive measurement.
